title: propositions
notes: A declarative statement of fact with a truth value — either true or false, never both.

title: negation
notes: It is not the case that p. Negation has the opposite truth value to p.

title: conjunction
notes: Both p and q must be true; false otherwise.

title: disjunction
notes: At least one is true, including when both are true. Or is inclusive by default.

title: xor
notes: Exactly one proposition is true, not both.

title: conditional
notes: Only when p is true and q is false: the condition is met but the result does not follow.

title: biconditional
notes: When p and q have the same truth value.

title: converse
notes: q → p.

title: contrapositive
notes: ¬q → ¬p. This is equivalent to the original implication.

title: allowed
notes: Only p → q ≡ ¬p ∨ q; p → q ≡ ¬q → ¬p; p ↔ q ≡ (p → q) ∧ (q → p). All of Table 6 is allowed. Other Table 7/8 identities must be derived.

title: tautology
notes: A compound proposition that is always true, no matter the truth values of its individual propositions.

title: universal
notes: For every x in the domain, P(x) is true.

title: existential
notes: There exists some (at least one) x in the domain so that P(x) is true.

title: distribution
notes: No. ∀x(P(x) ∨ Q(x)) ≢ ∀xP(x) ∨ ∀xQ(x). Different x may satisfy different predicates.

title: order
notes: Not in general. ∀x∃y allows y to depend on x; ∃y∀x requires one y for every x.

title: mp
notes: p → q, p, ∴ q.

title: validity
notes: Yes. Validity says that if all premises are true, the conclusion must be true.

title: even
notes: An integer n is even if there exists some integer k so that n = 2k.

title: odd
notes: An integer n is odd if there exists some integer k so that n = 2k + 1.

title: rational
notes: A real number x is rational if there exist integers p, q with q ≠ 0 so that x = p/q.

title: sets
notes: An unordered collection of distinct objects which we call elements.

title: power
notes: The set of all subsets of S. If |S| = n, then |P(S)| = 2ⁿ.

title: empty
notes: No. ∅ has 0 elements. {∅} has 1 element: the empty set.
